references.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: A Validity Audit of Tool-Calling Evaluation
references.manuscript_claim: Audits validity and reproducibility of BFCL v4, tau^2-Bench, LiveMCPBench and MCP-Atlas; 92 evaluator-human disagreements across 496 expert-reviewed tasks (18.5% misalignment); incorrect ground truths and brittle state matching among the failure modes; 23 repeated evaluations of one LiveMCPBench setup span 57.9-76.8%.
supporting_quotes: Across 496 expert-reviewed benchmark tasks, we find 92 evaluator-human disagreements, corresponding to an 18.5% misalignment rate
deterministic benchmarks exhibit brittle state matching, trajectory lock-in, incorrect ground truths, substring-based communication failures, and reward-basis misalignment
23 repeated evaluations of the same setup produce scores ranging from 57.9% to 76.8%
references.verification: arXiv abstract page retrieved and read on 2026-09-14. Title, full author list, submission date, primary category, and abstract confirmed. Every figure attributed to this work in the manuscript is quoted from that abstract.
references.relation_to_this_work: Closest prior work: same object (tool-calling benchmarks), same concern (the evaluator rather than the agent), same primary category. Distinguished in the manuscript by position in the pipeline -- their audit reads post-execution evidence and asks whether the score was right; ours runs before execution and asks whether the expected answer is determined. No priority claim is made over it.

references.title: Automated Transcript Analysis for Detecting Flaws in Agentic Benchmarks
references.manuscript_claim: AI scanners for four validity issues -- ground truth access, tool failure, guessing vulnerability, answer format ambiguity -- finding verified quality issues in five widely used benchmarks.
supporting_quotes: we developed AI scanners to detect four types of validity issues: ground truth access, tool failure, guessing vulnerability, and answer format ambiguity
Our scanners identified several verified quality issues in five widely used benchmarks
references.verification: arXiv abstract page retrieved and read on 2026-09-14. Title, full author list, submission date, primary category, and abstract confirmed. Every figure attributed to this work in the manuscript is quoted from that abstract.
references.relation_to_this_work: Their 'ground truth access' criterion is the mirror image of this paper's defect on the same axis: they scan for oracle information the agent should not be able to reach, we measure oracle information the agent cannot reach at all.

references.title: Automated Benchmark Auditing for AI Agents and Large Language Models
references.manuscript_claim: Agentic auditor over 168 benchmarks in nine domains; critical issues including ambiguous task design, execution environment conflicts and incorrect ground truths in over 25.7% of the EVALUATED TASKS; filtering shifts model rankings and raises average performance on SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2 by 9.9% and 9.6%.
supporting_quotes: ABA identifies critical issues including ambiguous task design, execution environment conflicts, and incorrect ground truths in over 25.7% of the evaluated tasks
filtering out these tasks with issues shifts model rankings and increases average performance on SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2 by 9.9% and 9.6%, respectively
references.verification: arXiv abstract page retrieved and read on 2026-09-14; re-read on 2026-09-16 to check the denominator of the 25.7% figure. Title, full author list, submission date, primary category, and abstract confirmed. Every figure attributed to this work in the manuscript is quoted from that abstract.
references.relation_to_this_work: Reports incorrect ground truths as a benchmark defect class at scale, which is why this manuscript makes no claim to be first to find that class. Also audits task design and execution-environment conflicts, i.e. properties of the task definition rather than of a trajectory, which is why manuscript version 3.3 withdrew the claim that existing audits are all post-execution.
references.correction_v33: Manuscript versions 3 through 3.2 attached the 25.7% to the 168 benchmarks ('find over 25.7% carrying critical issues' in a sentence whose subject was the benchmark count). The abstract states it as a share of evaluated TASKS. The supporting_quote recorded in this file was itself a paraphrase, not a quotation, and it is what carried the error forward. Corrected in manuscript version 3.3 and here. No number produced by this project is affected.

references.title: Do Androids Dream of Breaking the Game? Systematically Auditing AI Agent Benchmarks with BenchJack
references.manuscript_claim: Eight-pattern taxonomy of benchmark vulnerabilities; automated red-teaming across ten popular benchmarks uncovers 219 distinct flaws.
supporting_quotes: testing across ten popular benchmarks uncovered 219 distinct flaws
references.verification: arXiv abstract page retrieved and read on 2026-09-14. Title, full author list, submission date, primary category, and abstract confirmed. Every figure attributed to this work in the manuscript is quoted from that abstract.

references.verification: arXiv abstract page retrieved and read on 2026-09-14. Title, full author list, submission date, primary category, and abstract confirmed. A NeurIPS 2025 poster listing for this title appeared in search results but was not retrieved directly; the manuscript therefore cites the arXiv record, which was verified, and makes no venue claim.
references.relation_to_this_work: The canonical prior checklist for agentic benchmark rigour. Its scope is task and reward design broadly; this paper contributes one operational criterion inside that programme.

references.title: AgentSuite: Toward More Reliable Agent Evaluation with a Component-Based Benchmark Auditing Pipeline
references.manuscript_claim: The COBA pipeline decomposes an agent task into User, Environment, Ground Truth and Evaluation components and audits each with rule-based detectors and taxonomy-guided LLM evaluation, reporting F1 between 0.791 and 0.874 against expert assessment across six benchmarks.
supporting_quotes: modern agent benchmarks often contain hidden flaws arising from interactions among user instructions, environments, tools, ground-truth trajectories, and evaluation protocols
hybrid rule-based detectors and taxonomy-guided LLM evaluation
references.verification: ICML 2026 conference programme entry for the accepted poster retrieved and read on 2026-09-16; title, full author list and abstract read from it. Cross-checked against the ICML 2026 downloads index, which lists the same title and links the same poster page. No arXiv record for this work could be retrieved, and the camera copy was not read. This is a venue-level check, weaker than the publisher-PDF checks behind some other entries, and the manuscript cites the work only for its component decomposition and the F1 range its abstract states.
references.relation_to_this_work: COBA's Ground Truth component is the same object this paper audits, approached by taxonomy-guided LLM judgement where this work uses a declared finite derivation grammar and a deterministic per-item rule.

references.title: Beyond Local Accuracy: A Protocol-Level Identifiability Audit for Controlled LLM Reasoning Evaluation
references.manuscript_claim: Audits, before any model inference, whether an observation protocol's support can distinguish policies with different estimands; base-only observation collapses seven frozen deterministic policies into one equivalence class while full support yields seven classes with no cross-estimand collisions.
supporting_quotes: base-only observation collapses seven frozen deterministic policies into one equivalence class; full support yields seven classes and no cross-estimand collisions
evaluation-design validity can be checked structurally before model inference
references.verification: arXiv abstract page retrieved and read on 2026-09-16. Title, full author list, submission date, primary category, and abstract confirmed. Both quoted figures are from that abstract. Full text not read.
references.relation_to_this_work: The nearest prior work on the vocabulary this manuscript uses. It establishes structural identifiability auditing of an evaluation design before inference; this manuscript therefore claims no priority over pre-inference identifiability auditing. The units differ: Luo et al. ask whether a protocol separates policy classes with different estimands; this work asks whether one benchmark item's concrete expected target value is derivable from that item's granted information surface. Manuscript version 3.3 narrowed the contribution statement to the item-level question because of this work.

references.title: GeneBench: Assessing AI Agents for Multi-Stage Inference Problems in Genomics and Quantitative Biology
references.manuscript_claim: States the principle this manuscript audits as a benchmark-construction requirement rather than as an audit. Its primary design constraints open with a block titled 'Ground truth and identifiability' requiring that agents be graded on the quantity recoverable from agent-visible data rather than on hidden data-generating parameters, and that the staged evidence plus a minimum viable prompt support one uniquely defensible answer. Enforcement is at construction time: data are simulated so the correct answer is recoverable from the staged files, and independent review of target identifiability is part of problem development.
supporting_quotes: Agents are graded on recovering the quantity that is actually recoverable from agent-visible data, and not the hidden data-generating parameters.

The staged evidence along with a minimum viable prompt supports one uniquely defensible answer. If multiple approaches would ordinarily appear defensible, the data contain some empirical signature that rules out all but one.
The task becomes under-specified, and success depends on guessing the benchmark designer's preferred pipeline rather than reasoning from the evidence.
Data are then simulated so that the correct answer is recoverable from the staged files

Independent reviews for scientific validity, methodological soundness, and target identifiability are conducted in order to ensure that the evaluation is testing the intended capabilities rather than whether agents can guess the benchmark designer's preferred (but non-unique) workflow.
references.verification: Verified 2026-09-17 by three independent routes. (1) The DOI was resolved: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.22.720113 returned HTTP 302 to biorxiv.org/lookup/doi/10.64898/2026.04.22.720113. (2) The bioRxiv API record was retrieved from api.biorxiv.org/details/biorxiv/10.64898/2026.04.22.720113 and returned doi 10.64898/2026.04.22.720113, the title above, authors 'Li, J.; Ho, A.', date 2026-04-23, version 1, category genomics, published 'NA'. (3) The publisher-hosted PDF was retrieved from cdn.openai.com, its text extracted locally, and Table 1 ('Primary design constraints in GeneBench') and the problem-development paragraph read directly. Every supporting quote above is verbatim from that PDF. This is the only reference added in manuscript version 3, 3.3 or 3.4 whose content claim rests on a full text rather than on an abstract or a conference programme entry.
references.relation_to_this_work: The closest statement in the literature of this manuscript's own premise, and the reason version 3.4 withdraws any claim to introducing recoverability of a graded target from method-visible information as an evaluation concern. The difference is position in time and mechanism of decision: GeneBench designs identifiability into problems while they are under construction and confirms it by independent review; this manuscript tests whether it is present in an oracle that already exists, by a deterministic per-item rule over fields, literals and construction steps under a declared information-rights object and a finite derivation grammar, with the typed outcome of every item committed as an artifact. Supplied by an external review of the version 3.3 package, not found by the author's own literature search.

references.title: Agentic Generation of AST Transformation Rules for Fixing Breaking Updates

references.note_for_manuscript: The manuscript uses the 78.6% vs 33.3% contrast to make an argument of its own about transfer under reduced information. That argument is the authors' inference and is presented as such, not attributed to this work.

license_record.local_use: No third-party code or dataset is redistributed in this paper package; the references are bibliographic only.

residual_risk: One of nineteen references (assidiqi2026referencefree) carries an unverified content level. The manuscript's positioning against it is correspondingly weak and is marked as such in Appendix E.
Two references (chen2025toolevo, wu2026contda) were verified from abstracts rather than full text. The manuscript's claims about them are confined to statements the abstracts make directly.
No reference in this manuscript is cited for a numeric result that the manuscript itself compares against. All third-party figures quoted are contextual.

Version 3: the six benchmark-validity references added in this version were verified at abstract level only. Their titles, author lists, dates, categories and abstracts were read directly from arXiv; their full texts were not. They are cited for the claims their abstracts state and for positioning, not for methodological detail. This is a weaker standard than the full-text checks behind some version 2 references, and it is recorded here rather than left implicit.

Version 3.3: three references were added (tu2026benchguard, suh2026agentsuite, luo2026identifiability) after an external review found that the version 3 literature search had missed the pre-execution and identifiability framings, which is where the two closest works sit. All three were verified at abstract level; suh2026agentsuite was verified from its ICML 2026 conference programme entry rather than a publisher PDF or an arXiv record, which is the weakest metadata route used anywhere in this file, and is recorded as such in its own entry. The same review found that this file's supporting_quote for wang2026autoaudit was a paraphrase rather than a quotation, and that the paraphrase had dropped the denominator of the 25.7% figure; the quote is now verbatim from the abstract and the manuscript sentence is corrected.

Version 3.4: one reference was added (li2026genebench) after an external review of the version 3.3 package found that the closest published statement of this manuscript's own premise sits inside a genomics and quantitative-biology benchmark, which neither the version 3 nor the version 3.3 literature search reached. Two consecutive releases have now had their closest related work supplied by a reader rather than by the author's search. That is a property of the search scope, and no later search has been run that would justify claiming the literature is now complete.
